  - **Action**: #5182 [BUG] config/wireguard: IPv6 WireGuard peers hydrated RESPONDER-ONLY because the lexer stripped the port from a bracketed `[v6]:port` endpoint. The lexer consumes `[`/`]` as bracket-list sugar (#2419), so `endpoint [2001:db8::1]:51820` split into a bare host `2001:db8::1` plus an orphan `:51820`; only the port-less host reached peer.Endpoint. endpointIsV6 leniently accepted the bare IP, so it COMMITTED CLEAN, and the Rust hydrate `wg_endpoint.parse::<SocketAddr>()` returned None on the port-less host → peer.endpoint None → the peer could never initiate handshakes/keepalives. Fix, three layers: (1) lexer tryBracketedEndpointLiteral recognizes `[<identrun>]:` and emits the whole `[addr]:port` as ONE identifier token (both AST shapes share the lexer) — narrow match (whitespace after `[`, or `[x]` without a trailing `:`, both fall through to strip) so it never collides with a genuine `[ a b c ]` list; (2) endpointIsV6 (strict commit gate) now REQUIRES net.SplitHostPort + numeric port in 1..65535 + IP-literal host — rejects port-less/zero-port/hostname endpoints so the commit-accept set never exceeds what the dataplane can hydrate; (3) Rust hydrate_wg_identity DROPS the row on a non-empty unparseable endpoint (fail-closed) instead of coercing to None/responder-only (defense-in-depth for leniently-loaded configs). Tests: (Go) TestWireguardV6EndpointPortPreserved{FlatSet,Hierarchical} pin the full `[addr]:port` through compile (RED on lexer revert — verified), TestWireguardEndpointMissingPortRejected rejects bare v6/v4 + `:0`, TestWireguardV6EndpointAccepted; (Rust) wg_endpoint_v6_bracketed_hydrates_initiator_capable proves Some(SocketAddr) with the port, wg_endpoint_nonempty_unparseable_drops_row proves the row is dropped (RED on `.parse().ok()` revert). docs/config-schema.md WG section documents the endpoint format contract + the port requirement.

The package header explicitly claimed "no migration pass". Fix: added Journal.migratePermsLocked() (guarded by a new `migrated` bool, runs once under j.mu on first Log OR Tail) which lstat+chmods every OWNED segment (current + rotation siblings .1../.N) to 0600 before first use; chmodOwnerOnly() only ever TIGHTENS (a 0600-or-stricter file is left alone — a 0400 file is not loosened), REFUSES to follow a symlink (lstat, never chmod through it to an arbitrary target), skips non-regular/missing paths, and surfaces a chmod/lstat failure as slog.Warn rather than swallowing it. maybeRotateLocked now re-asserts chmodOwnerOnly on the renamed .1 so rotation never widens exposure. Updated the package header + pkg/configstore/README.md journal paragraph/table to document the append-mode gap and the migration/repair pass (contrasting the fsatomic inode-replacing DB files that self-heal on next commit). Tests (journal_test.go): preexisting-0644-current migrated via Log; 0644 rotated .1 migrated via Tail (proves the read path also repairs); rotation-repair isolated via a direct maybeRotateLocked call; single-rotation end-to-end through Log; symlink-target-untouched guard; 0400-stays-0400 tightening-only guard.   - **Action**: #5110 [BUG] daemon/snmp: the default SNMP serve closure discarded Agent.Start's error (incl. a UDP/161 bind failure) and reconcileSNMP recorded the desired-config hash immediately after launch with no readiness signal, so a transient bind failure left SNMP absent while the hash recorded "applied" — every identical later apply took the idempotent no-op path (hash matches) and SNMP stayed silently down until a config change/restart. Test (TestReconcileSNMPBindFailureLeavesHashUnrecordedAndRetries, snmpServeBindOutcome seam scripting a first-attempt bind failure then success): asserts a failed bind leaves d.snmpAgent nil + snmpHashSet false, and the next identical apply retries the bind (attempts 1->2), self-heals, and records the hash; RED on revert (verified — recording the hash on the failed start trips the "SNMP stays silently down" assertion).   **Action**: #4899 [BUG] daemon/ipsec: the runtime DHCP-lease-change IPsec rebind path (`reapplyIPsecForLeaseChange`, management-only branch of `onDHCPAddressChange`) DROPPED swanctl reload failures as a bare `slog.Warn` — no retry, no dirty flag, no health signal. When a DHCP renewal moved the address on an `external-interface`-bound uplink (no explicit `local-address`, `HasDHCPBoundGateway` true), a failed `swanctl --load-all` left strongSwan binding the STALE lease address, the tunnel could not re-establish, and the operator had no signal and no recovery. Fix makes the failure RECOVERABLE + VISIBLE, mirroring the probe-pin retry idiom (#1895, `probePinRetryLoop`): on failure the daemon raises an `ipsecRebindPending` flag and arms a single-flight retry loop (`ipsecRebindRetryLoop`, `daemon_ipsec_rebind.go`) that re-renders+reloads against the LIVE active config (`d.store.ActiveConfig` — so a commit that removes the VPN/DHCP binding converges the loop instead of resurrecting deleted config) on a 30s cadence until it converges, then clears the flag and disarms. Both the apply and the pending-flag transition run under the apply semaphore, so the pending state always reflects the last completed apply (no lost-failure race vs a concurrent commit's IPsec apply). Health signal: new `xpf_ipsec_rebind_pending` Prometheus gauge (0/1) surfaced via `Daemon.IPsecRebindPending` → `api.Config.IPsecRebindPendingFn`, mirroring `xpf_frr_reload_degraded` (#1880). The lease callback stays NON-FATAL to lease processing (retry + gauge ARE the recovery). Commit-path IPsec apply (already fail-closes the commit, #4433) unchanged. Tests: `TestReapplyIPsecForLeaseChange_FailureArmsRetryAndSetsHealth` (pending SET + retry armed + loop re-invokes apply >=2x — RED on warn-only revert, verified), `_RecoveryClearsHealth` (pending SET after fail then CLEARS after success + loop disarms — RED on revert), `_NonFatalToLeaseProcessing` (callback returns promptly on failure, healthy apply arms nothing); `TestIPsecRebindPendingGauge` (pkg/api, gauge tracks fn + emits with dataplane unloaded) + descriptor-coverage fixture/sentinel wiring. Validation: `go build ./...` exit 0; `go test ./pkg/daemon/... ./pkg/ipsec/... ./pkg/api/...` ok (daemon suite also -race clean); gofmt clean. pkg/ipsec/README.md #2884 section extended with the #4899 retry + health-signal contract.

  **Action**: #5282 [HIGH security] feeds: `Manager.Apply` called `StopAll` as its FIRST step, replacing `m.feeds` with an EMPTY map (dropping every installed snapshot) before the desired plan's producers fetched asynchronously. So editing a deny feed's URL/interval compiled the overlay to match-NONE from that instant until the new fetch landed — and if the new endpoint was down, `retainForever` (the #2050 default) pinned the EMPTY set indefinitely: a fail-OPEN denylist window where traffic that should be DENIED was ALLOWED, contradicting #2050's "never fail-open a stale denylist". Fix: `Apply` builds the desired plan first, then swaps the producer set under one lock — cancels every old producer (each captured its old URL/interval, so a persisted feed with an edited URL/interval needs a fresh refresh loop) but carries each PERSISTED feed's (same name) last-good enforced snapshot forward into the replacement `feedState` (`carryForwardSnapshot`: prefixes/hash/hasSnapshot/lastFetch/lastSuccess/invalid* deep-copied under lock; LastError/StaleSince intentionally reset so the new endpoint gets a clean slate + a fresh hold window). Persisted feed keeps enforcing last-good until its NEW fetch atomically replaces it (installSnapshot); a REMOVED feed has no plan entry so its snapshot is dropped (correct); a brand-NEW feed starts empty (documented cold-start). `StopAll` retained for the shutdown path only. #4913 dedup plan + #5202/#5036 reconcile gate preserved. Tests (fail-on-revert): `TestApplyReconfigureFailedFetchRetainsLastGood` (core fail-open guard — persisted feed + failed reconfigure fetch keeps last-good via GetPrefixes AND SnapshotForBindings overlay; RED on revert to StopAll-drops-all, verified: "Apply dropped last-good for a persisted feed: got [], want [203.0.113.0/24]"), `TestApplyDropsRemovedFeed` (removed→nil, persisted→retained), `TestApplyReconfigureSuccessfulFetchReplacesSnapshot` (atomic swap replaces carried set).   **Action**: #5270 [BUG] config/bgp: BGP group inheritance was sibling-ORDER-DEPENDENT. compileProtocols walked a group's children ONCE and stamped each neighbor with whatever group-level defaults had been seen SO FAR, so a `neighbor` authored before the group's `export`/`peer-as`/etc. captured the empty/zero default (e.g. neighbor-before-`export OUT` → empty Export → FRR emits no outbound route-map → outbound route leak, fail-open, not vSRX-equivalent). The order dependency hit both AST shapes (hierarchical block + flat-set). Fix: a two-pass, order-INDEPENDENT group walk — pass 0 processes every NON-neighbor child, fully collecting ALL inheritable group defaults (peer-as/local-as/local-address/hold-time/passive/description/multihop/export/import/family+prefix-limit/authentication-key/bfd/default-originate/loops/remove-private; list leaves accumulate via firewallMatchValues); pass 1 processes only `neighbor` children, stamping each from the completed defaults. Per-neighbor explicit values still OVERRIDE the inherited group default (precedence unchanged; only the DEFAULT source moved from seen-so-far to fully-collected). Same compileProtocols runs for top-level `protocols bgp` and per-routing-instance BGP, so both inherit the fix. Semantic diff is only the `for pass` wrapper + two guard-continues; the rest of the neighbor block is pure gofmt reindent (one deeper nesting level). Tests (bgp_group_inherit_order_5270_test.go): neighbor-before-export inherits Export (RED on single-pass revert — verified: Export=[] vs [OUT]), export-before-neighbor regression guard, both orders IDENTICAL across export/peer-as/local-address/hold-time, per-neighbor override still wins in both orders, neighbor-before-peer-as inherits (RED on revert — single-pass rejects remote-as 0), plus a hierarchical-shape variant (RED on revert). - **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
  **Action**: #5285 [SECURITY/BUG] ddns/surface-a: the Surface A publish path had a save→wire crash window that falsely confirmed a renumber and LOST the prior DNS value. publishLocked persisted the DESIRED address into the SOLE ownership row BEFORE the provider I/O with NO durable pending bit and NO retained prior value (the in-process rollback only runs on an error return, never on a crash). A kill between `state.save(B)` and `providerIO(UpsertLease)` seeded B as BOTH `lastAddr` and successfully-published: on restart `seedFromStore` seeded B, the `owned && !changed && !refreshDue` skip suppressed recovery, public DNS stayed at the OLD value A while the appliance reported B, and A's value-specific cleanup key was destroyed. Fix mirrors the DHCP-lease `PTRPending` durable-pending idiom: added durable `ownedRecord.PublishPending` + `PriorAddrText` (state.go). publishLocked now write-aheads `{desired=B, PublishPending=true, prior=<last confirmed A>}` BEFORE the wire op and CONFIRMS it (clears the pending bit, releases the prior value) with a second save AFTER a successful wire add. reconcileScopeLocked forces `refreshDue` while a record is PENDING (`pendingRecovery`), so restart RE-RUNS the wire op for the desired value and threads the retained prior A as `PrevAddr` (value-specific in-place replace of xpf's real live value, never the phantom desired). prevAddr resolution honors the pending case (reads PriorAddrText, not the un-confirmed AddrText). In-process rollback (NON-crash wire failure restores the confirmed prior) preserved — the durable pending bit is the crash-safe superset. DISTINCT from #2662 (end-of-pass orphan window; records desired as though confirmed). Tests (surface_a_durable_pending_5285_test.go): crash-recovery via a panic-on-UpsertLease backend (faithful kill between save and wire) proves restart detects PENDING, re-runs the wire for B, retains A as PrevAddr, and does NOT report B confirmed/skip — RED on revert to the no-pending-bit save-desired-first behavior (verified: the crash leaves {AddrText=B, PublishPending=false, PriorAddrText=""}, failing the must-be-PENDING assertion); happy-path A→B confirms + releases A; in-process rollback still restores prevOwned. Validation: go build ./... exit 0; go test ./pkg/ddns/... ok (new tests also -race clean); gofmt clean. pkg/ddns/README.md Surface A engine section documents the durable desired-vs-confirmed crash-recovery contract + the #2662 distinction.

  **Action**: #5284 [HIGH upgrade-safety] pkg/upgrade: a bare `xpfd upgrade` (no `--rolling`) ran an UNCOORDINATED standalone STOP->FLIP->START cut on a CLUSTERED node — there was no node-id gate. #4869 only rejects leftover POSITIONAL args, so a VALID empty arg set still selected `Runner.Run` purely because `--rolling` was omitted, and rollback begins only AFTER the unit is already stopped — so on a clustered primary `Runner.Run` reached `StopUnit` after only the host-local upgrade lock, with NO peer/RG-ownership transfer or peer-readiness fence -> outage/blackhole on a not-ready peer. The recovery docs and the postinst deferred-publish branch emitted the bare verb too. Fix: enforce the invariant at the FINAL privileged boundary — a cluster gate at the TOP of `Runner.Run` (BEFORE the host-wide lock, BEFORE any journal read or StopUnit): if the cluster-identity marker `/etc/xpf/node-id` is PRESENT and `opts.ClusterCoordinated` is false, refuse (`refuse-standalone-cut-on-clustered-node`) with guidance to run `xpfd upgrade --rolling`; fail CLOSED (no auto-reroute), unit NOT stopped. Presence — not content — is the signal (mirrors pkg/daemon hasNodeIDFile; pkg/upgrade can't import pkg/daemon: cycle, so the /etc/xpf/node-id path is duplicated as DefaultNodeIDFile + a test-overridable Config.NodeIDPath seam). New Options.ClusterCoordinated is set EXCLUSIVELY by runRollingWith (rolling.go) so the coordinated per-node cut — run AFTER ForceSecondary + the strong drain predicate — bypasses the gate and rolling upgrades are NOT blocked. Belt-and-suspenders: cmd/xpfd/upgrade.go rejects early before building the Runner. Tests (cutover_cluster_gate_5284_test.go, fail-on-revert): node-id PRESENT + bare cut -> REFUSED, StopUnit NEVER called (asserted via fake unit-stopper call log), unit still running, no journal persisted, current unmoved; node-id ABSENT + bare cut -> proceeds (StopUnit called, flips to 2.0.0); rolling driver on a clustered node -> cut completes (drop-in written, current->2.0.0), NOT blocked. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: neutralizing the gate makes the clustered-reject test fail ("expected the clustered-node cut to be refused, got nil" — the cut ran STOPPED->FLIPPED->STARTED->COMMITTED). Validation: GOCACHE/GOTMPDIR go build ./... exit 0; go test ./cmd/xpfd/... ./pkg/upgrade/... ok; gofmt clean; test/debian/postinst-test.sh PASS. Docs: docs/in-place-upgrade.md gains a "Clustered-node standalone-cut invariant (#5284)" paragraph + node-id-aware deferred-publish recovery; debian/xpf.postinst deferred/failed-publish recovery hints now emit `$CUT_HINT` (`xpfd upgrade --rolling` on a clustered node).

  **Action**: #5311 [BUG vsrx-parity] eventengine: the arm-on-commit cooldown stamp was revision-BLIND. `runAction` called `armCooldown(name)` after a successful commit and `armCooldown` stamped `e.runtime[name].lastTrigger` with NO identity check, while `Apply` installs a FRESH `newPolicyRuntime()` (zero lastTrigger) whenever `semRev` changes. Name-based ABA: a remediation whose own action redefines its triggering policy (R1→R2) commits synchronously → the daemon commit callback reconciles the new config and calls `Engine.Apply`, which installs the successor R2's fresh re-armed runtime → then `armCooldown(name)` stamps R2 with R1's completion time → the re-armed R2 is SUPPRESSED for the whole ~30s cooldown, undoing the reconcile's re-arm and contradicting the documented "a redefined policy re-arms" contract. Fix: pass the authorizing semantic revision (`plannedAction.semRev`) into `armCooldown(name, authRev)`; stamp ONLY when `e.semRev[name] == authRev` (live runtime is still the same generation that authorized the action). If a successor was installed (semRev changed) or the policy was removed (no entry), skip the stamp so the successor keeps its zero/re-armed lastTrigger. The identity check + stamp run together under `e.mu` so a concurrent `Apply` cannot swap the runtime between them (no TOCTOU). Normal (non-self-modifying) path unchanged: authRev still matches the carried-forward runtime → stamps as before; cooldown duration unchanged. Distinct from #3750/#5063/#5062/#2140. Tests (engine_cooldown_rev_5311_test.go): `TestArmCooldown_SkipsSuccessorGeneration_5311` (unit, deterministic — models the reconcile, arms with R1's rev, asserts successor R2 lastTrigger stays zero; RED on revert to the name-only stamp, VERIFIED), `TestCooldown_SelfRedefinedSuccessorFires_5311` (e2e through the worker — commit callback reconciles R2 via Apply; the immediate re-fire commits (Committed reaches 2, host-name gen3); RED on revert via commit-count timeout, VERIFIED), plus normal-case guards `TestArmCooldown_StampsSameGeneration_5311` and `TestCooldown_NormalPolicyRapidRefireSuppressed_5311`. Validation: `go build ./...` exit 0; `go test -count=1 ./pkg/eventengine/...` ok; `-race` clean; gofmt clean. Docs: engine.go package contract gains a #5311 bullet; pkg/eventengine/README.md gains a "Revision-aware cooldown arm (#5311)" section.

  **Action**: #5299 [BUG vsrx-parity] config/firewall: the legacy single-rate two-color policer leaves `firewall policer <name> if-exceeding bandwidth-limit` / `burst-size-limit` were untyped (`ValueAny`), so the compiler's silent-zero parsers coerced garbage / zero / overflow to 0. A typo like `if-exceeding bandwidth-limit 10mm` COMMITTED CLEAN → `parseBandwidthLimit` returned 0 bps → the userspace runtime `fail_closed(true)` (#4522/#4514) drop-alls matching traffic for the default `then discard` (or inerts the meter for non-discard) — a silent total outage invisible at commit. `parseBurstSizeLimit` was additionally an unchecked `v * multiplier` uint64 multiply that WRAPPED an overflowing burst to a small nonzero value (a silently-wrong meter). Fix (fail-closed, #1960 doctrine): `bandwidth-limit` typed `ValueRate` + `ValidateRate` (rejects empty/malformed/negative/NaN/Inf/overflow/<8bps, folding in 0); `burst-size-limit` typed `ValueByteSize` + a new `ValidatePolicerBurstSize` (rejects empty/zero/negative/malformed/overflow via `parseBurstSizeLimitStrict`, but ACCEPTS a bare integer since a bare byte count is unambiguous for a policer bucket and was valid-compiling input). The lenient `parseBurstSizeLimit` now delegates to `parseBurstSizeLimitStrict` and returns 0 on error, so overflow is no longer wrapped to a nonzero meter — it becomes the unambiguous 0 the strict schema gate already rejects. Tolerant `Store.Load` / `SyncApply` (`compileTreeLenient`) runs the SAME `SchemaValidate` gate but DOWNGRADES to a warning + compiles leniently (coerce to 0), so a peer-synced / older-binary policer cannot blackout-boot. NO compiled-`FirewallConfig` strict gate added: `SchemaValidate` runs on the fully apply-groups-expanded tree so every strict-commit form is covered at the schema leaf; the only schema-leaf-bypassing paths are the tolerant ingress that #1960 requires to stay lenient (verified `validateThreeColorPolicersStrict` hard-fails even under `CompileConfigLenient` — a contrasting latent-brick precedent deliberately not replicated; a compiled `BandwidthLimit == 0` also can't be distinguished from a legit-unset limit without a `Configured` bool the type lacks). Tests (`policer_rate_validate_5299_test.go`, flat-set `ParseSetCommand`+`SetPath`): valid `10m`/`15k`/bare-int accept + compile-to-expected-units, malformed/zero/negative/NaN/Inf/overflow strict-REJECT, tolerant-load WARN-not-hard-fail, direct `parseBurstSizeLimit` overflow-returns-0. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: reverting the schema validators makes every reject case commit clean (`got nil`); reverting the `parseBurstSizeLimit` delegation makes the overflow test RED (`20000000000000g` → wrapped `3729424098846048256`).   **Action**: #5307 [BUG dataplane] The userspace-shim deploy pre-flight (`xpfd verify-dataplane` -> `validateUserspaceShimSpec`, run BEFORE stopping the old daemon per README #1864 §3) checked only presence + `MaxEntries` (+ a `NO_PREALLOC` flag) for three maps. Production enables `PinByName`, so an ABI edit that keeps `MaxEntries` (a key/value-size change, a map-type change, or a flag change) passed the green pre-flight, the old daemon was stopped, and the new daemon's `NewCollectionWithOptions` then failed `ErrMapIncompatible` — stranding the node fail-closed (config-only), the exact shape #1864 aims to prevent. Distinct from #4976/#4977. Fix: extend `validateUserspaceShimSpec` (moved body to `validateUserspaceShimSpecWith(spec, reader)` with an injectable live-pin reader) to compare — for every PinByName shim map — the embedded shim's `Type`/`KeySize`/`ValueSize`/`MaxEntries`/`Flags` (the exact fields cilium/ebpf `MapSpec.Compatible` flags with `ErrMapIncompatible`) against BOTH the Go-side expected shape (dnat_table via `userspaceShimSharedMapSpecs`, new `validateDNATExpectedABI`) AND the RUNNING daemon's LIVE pinned maps (read-only `ebpf.LoadPinnedMap` + shape accessors, `readPinnedShimMapABI`). This moves the `ErrMapIncompatible` failure from the post-stop LOAD to the pre-stop pre-flight, so the deploy is refused with the old dataplane still forwarding. No pin yet (fresh node) -> live-pin arm skipped (only expected-value checks apply, no false-fail); the disposable `userspace_fallback_stats` counter is excluded from the ABI check (reconciled/reset on the #4113 shape change — ABI-checking it would re-brick that upgrade). The gate enumerates names with the SAME `namedInstances` helper the compiler keys the maps with, so it checks exactly the colliding names. Fix: build the message path from `vrrpGroupIDKeys(n)` (value-free `vrrp-group <id>` identity) before feeding `checkVRRPGroupTrackShape` — mirrors the identical guard the #4288 auth validator already uses.   **Action**: #4923 [BUG flowexport] The packet-count fallback for the exported flow StartTime (`flowStartTime`, `Created==0` path) computed `rec.Time.Add(-estimateSessionDuration(rec.SessionPkts, proto))` with NO overflow guard. `estimateSessionDuration` multiplies the uint64 packet count by a per-packet time (100ms TCP / 50ms non-TCP); above ~92.2B TCP packets (~184.5B non-TCP) the product overflowed signed `time.Duration` NEGATIVE, and subtracting a negative duration moved StartTime AFTER EndTime — first-switched after last-switched (NetFlow) / contradictory absolute ms (IPFIX) that collectors may reject, on the legacy/HA-recovery fallback paths. The real-`created` branch already clamps future stamps to EndTime; the fallback did not. Fix: (1) `estimateSessionDuration` now SATURATES at a new `maxEstimatedSessionAge` const (366d — a defensible session ceiling ~9e12 ns below the int64 nanosecond limit) so the estimate is always bounded and non-negative; the pre-cap-threshold path keeps the EXACT prior estimate (only the pathological overflow regime changes). (2) `flowStartTime` additionally clamps the fallback StartTime to EndTime (mirroring the `Created` skew clamp) so `StartTime <= EndTime` holds regardless of heuristic evolution. Tests (flowstart_test.go): `TestEstimateSessionDurationSaturates` (counts through math.MaxUint64, TCP+UDP, asserts 0 <= d <= cap and exact-cap saturation); `TestFlowStartTimeFallbackNeverAfterEnd` (Created==0 + 1e11/MaxUint64 pkts, asserts !start.After(end) and non-negative duration). RED-on-revert VERIFIED: reverting the fix logic (const kept so tests compile) → `estimateSessionDuration(1e11,6) = -2346317h...` (negative overflow) and StartTime `2291-07-15` after EndTime `2023-11-14` — both tests FAIL; restored to green.   **Action**: #5057 [BUG,SECURITY pkg/api + pkg/grpcapi] The diagnostic REST/gRPC ping/traceroute endpoints spawned one child process (plus pipes, buffered output, a handler goroutine and — on gRPC — a stream) per request with ONLY a per-request deadline (`pingExecTimeout`/`diagTracerouteTimeout` + `WaitDelay`) and NO aggregate concurrency bound. The only admission control in pkg/api was the Prometheus `MaxRequestsInFlight` (metrics only). A burst of concurrent diagnostic requests could therefore hold hundreds/thousands of PIDs/FDs/goroutines for up to the 150s `diagExecCeiling`, a management-plane DoS that starves the control plane driving the dataplane. Fix: added a shared fail-fast counting semaphore `diagcmd.Limiter` + process-wide `diagcmd.DefaultLimiter` (`MaxConcurrentDiagnostics = 4`) in a new `pkg/diagcmd/limiter.go`. BOTH the REST handlers (`pingHandler`/`tracerouteHandler`) and the gRPC RPCs (`Ping`/`Traceroute`) acquire a slot before spawning any child, via a `diagLimiter` package var pointing at the same `DefaultLimiter` — so ONE aggregate cap covers BOTH surfaces (a diagnostic admitted over REST and one over gRPC draw from the same budget). Acquire is non-blocking: when the cap is reached the request is rejected immediately — REST returns HTTP 429, gRPC returns `codes.ResourceExhausted` — rather than queuing. The slot is released via `defer` on EVERY path (success, exec error, ctx timeout/cancel, panic); release is idempotent (`sync.Once`) so an accidental double-defer cannot over-release and free another caller's slot. Test seams added: `diagRun` (REST) and `streamDiag` (gRPC) package vars let tests inject a fake slow diagnostic without real ping/traceroute subprocesses. Tests: `pkg/diagcmd/limiter_test.go` (cap+reject semantics, idempotent release, N+K concurrent fake-diagnostic bound with an all-attempted barrier); `pkg/api/diag_concurrency_5057_test.go` + `pkg/grpcapi/diag_concurrency_5057_test.go` (fire cap+excess concurrent requests, assert ≤cap concurrent + excess rejected with 429/ResourceExhausted + fully-released-after-drain, plus a ping-holds-slot→concurrent-traceroute-rejected shared-limiter test). RED-on-revert VERIFIED: neutering the `diagLimiter.Acquire()` branch in both handler sides → REST `429 count = 0, want 5 [200 200 200 200 200 200 200]` and gRPC `ResourceExhausted count = 0, want 5 [<nil> ×7]` (all 7 admitted) — both main tests FAIL; restored to green. Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; go vet clean; `go test ./pkg/diagcmd/... ./pkg/api/... ./pkg/grpcapi/...` ok (new tests green under `-race -count=5`); gofmt clean. Docs: pkg/api/README.md + pkg/grpcapi/README.md diagnostic-endpoint sections document the shared limiter, the 429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED behavior, and release-on-all-paths. No cluster smoke (control-plane API, no forwarding path).

  **Action**: #5063 [BUG eventengine, codex-review-177 A9-b1-F4 Medium] The event-options commit classifier miscounted an active, dataplane-armed remediation commit as REJECTED. The daemon's CommitFn (commitAndApply -> applyAndSyncCommitted, daemon_apply.go) is TRI-STATE: on a NON-FATAL best-effort subsystem apply error (networkd write / Kea restart / host-inbound nft, #4034) it returns the just-committed *config.Config ALONGSIDE the error — the config is committed, active, and the dataplane armed. But applyOnce (pkg/eventengine/engine.go) discarded `compiled` and returned errBatch for ANY err, and runAction incremented `committed`/armed the cooldown only on err==nil, so a live autonomous change was counted rejected, no cooldown was armed, and the same event could immediately re-commit — false telemetry plus control-plane churn during an incident. Fix: applyOnce now reads the returned *config.Config (not the error) as the authority on promotion — a non-nil compiled with an error is signalled as a new `commitDebtError` (wraps the subsystem error, Unwrap exposed); runAction detects it via errors.As FIRST, counts `committed` + a distinct new `committedWithDebt` counter, arms the SAME-generation cooldown (#5311 authRev), logs a WARN, and does NOT retry. Only a nil compiled (commit never promoted / dataplane disarmed) remains a genuine rejection. Surfaced the debt subset as `xpf_event_actions_committed_with_debt_total` (pkg/api metrics.go/metrics_descriptors.go/metrics_system.go); `xpf_event_actions_committed_total` now documents it INCLUDES the debt subset. New callback-matrix fail-on-revert tests (pkg/eventengine/engine_armed_debt_5063_test.go): active-with-nonfatal-error -> committed+debt+cooldown-armed+active-config-updated (the CORE RED-on-revert case); genuine rejection (nil compiled) -> rejected, cooldown NOT armed, config unchanged; clean commit -> committed, zero debt; stale action -> droppedStale, never committed/rejected. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: temporarily reverting applyOnce to discard compiled + return errBatch made the debt commit log "remediation rejected", Committed stayed 0, and TestCommitDebt_ActiveWithNonfatalError_CountsCommitted_5063 timed out -> FAIL (other three still passed); restored to green.   **Action**: #5058 [BUG api/Server.Run listener leak] — Server.Run started HTTP and HTTPS in goroutines reporting to a shared errCh, and `select { case err := <-errCh: return err }` returned BEFORE the Shutdown block. A bind/serve failure of one listener while the other served successfully returned immediately and left the surviving listener serving forever (an orphaned management socket the daemon wrapper drops ownership of, never reaching the shutdown path).   **Action**: #5373 [BUG config security] `expandMemberRange` (pkg/config/compiler_interface_range.go) expanded a `member-range <start> to <end>` selector with a counting loop `for i := sn; i <= en; i++`. `sn`/`en` come from `splitTrailingInt`→`strconv.Atoi` (accepts up to math.MaxInt64; member-range tokens bypass typed-schema validation). The `interfaceRangeMaxMembers=4096` cap only bounds the DIFFERENCE `en-sn`, not `en`'s absolute value, so a range whose endpoints sit just below MaxInt64 (e.g. sn=MaxInt64-5, en=MaxInt64; en-sn=5 < cap) PASSES the guard yet overflows the loop: at i==MaxInt64 the body ran, then i++ wrapped to MinInt64, MinInt64<=MaxInt64 stayed true, and the loop appended member names forever → infinite loop + unbounded slice growth → OOM. Runs at strict commit AND on tolerant/HA config-sync load, so a persisted or peer-synced config hangs the daemon on load (fail-closed/HA-DoS), not merely on interactive commit. This is a DISTINCT overflow from #4807 (which guarded the `en-sn+1` capacity/negative-make panic for ranges that EXCEED the cap). Fix: iterate on the bounded COUNT — `n := en-sn` (guaranteed < interfaceRangeMaxMembers by the existing cap check), `for k := 0; k <= n; k++ { append(sp + fmt(sn+k)) }`. `k` stays small regardless of `en`'s magnitude; `sn+k` yields exactly sn..en (sn+n==en, every sn+k<=en<=MaxInt64 overflow-free). Cap semantics and the sn>en / prefix-mismatch rejections are unchanged. New test TestExpandMemberRangeNearMaxInt64Terminates drives expandMemberRange (sn=MaxInt64-5, en=MaxInt64) in a goroutine guarded by a `select{ case <-done: case <-time.After(2s): t.Fatal }` watchdog and asserts the bounded 6-name sn..en list with no warning; with the fix it returns instantly, without it the goroutine spins and the watchdog fires — RED on revert without wedging `go test`. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: ran the new test against unpatched code in isolation (`-run` + GOMEMLIMIT=1500MiB) → watchdog fired at 2.00s, FAIL, process exited cleanly at 2.038s (no box OOM); with the fix the full pkg/config suite passes in 1.459s (no hang). Docs: updated docs/config-schema.md #4027 entry to record the bounded-count iteration and why it differs from the #4807 capacity guard. Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; `go test ./pkg/config/...` ok (1.459s); gofmt clean. No cluster smoke (control-plane config-compilation path, no forwarding effect).

Every sibling mutator (Set/Delete/Deactivate/Activate/Copy/Rename/Insert/Load*/Rollback/ConfirmCommit) enforces ownership via a session-scoped `*As` variant that calls `ensureHolderLocked(sessionID)` (#5059); Annotate had no `AnnotateAs` variant at all, so a session-scoped caller could not annotate under holder enforcement, and the structural bypass (annotate another session's candidate + extend the true holder's idle lease) had no guard. REST (`configAnnotateHandler`) and the in-process CLI `annotate` dispatch keep calling the plain `Annotate` (sessionID==""), bit-identical to before and consistent with how those same transports already call the plain `SetFromInput`/`DeleteFromInput`; a non-holder session id is now rejected with `ErrConfigLockedByOther`, the identical sentinel the siblings return. Annotate is NOT wired to gRPC, so no handler needed threading; the `*As` variant exists so a future gRPC annotate handler gets enforcement for free like its siblings. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: deleting the `ensureHolderLocked` call from `AnnotateAs` made the dedicated test report `AnnotateAs(non-holder) = <nil>` (bypass reproduced) and the enforcement-table row report `path not found` (guard skipped, reached AnnotatePath) → both FAIL; restored → green.   **Action**: #5389 [BUG ddns/route53 MEDIUM] `route53Backend.UpsertLease` issued a bare full-RRset UPSERT — Route 53 `UPSERT` create-or-replaces the ENTIRE resource-record set at name+type, so a single-value change batch silently DELETED any co-resident FOREIGN A/AAAA (a manually-managed round-robin member, or another host's A at the same FQDN). This was the Route 53 arm of #3739 (Cloudflare + RFC 2136 were fixed; Route 53 was deferred as M07 and never implemented). Fix (ownership-scoped read-modify-write, mirroring the Cloudflare/RFC 2136 value-specific replace): both publish and withdraw now first `ListResourceRecordSets`-read the live RRset (new `listRRSet` + `listRRSetsXML`; a SigV4-signed GET with an EXACT name+type match so a Route 53 lexically-next neighbour set reads back as found=false) and change ONLY xpf's own value. `UpsertLease`: `mergeUpsertValues` keeps every current member except xpf's own prior value (`rec.PrevAddr`), adds `rec.Addr`, and UPSERTs the merged set — a live set already equal to the desired one (values + TTL) is a no-op; a first publish onto a foreign name is additive; a renumber with a lost prior value leaks a stale xpf row rather than clobbering a foreign one. `DeleteLease`: strip `rec.Addr` from the live set — absent set / xpf-value-absent ⇒ idempotent no-op (no change issued); foreign members remain ⇒ UPSERT the reduced set at the LIVE TTL; xpf's value sole member ⇒ DELETE the whole RRset (exact live-TTL match). The #2771 already-gone-DELETE idempotency (`r53DeleteAlreadyGone`) is preserved for the residual race where the record disappears between the List and the whole-RRset DELETE. `buildChangeBatch`/`change` generalized to take an explicit value list + TTL. CONCURRENCY CAVEAT documented in code + PR: Route 53 has no compare-and-swap for `ChangeResourceRecordSets`, so the RMW is not atomic — a foreign member written between the List and the change is not observed; the Surface A per-RG HA gate makes xpf a single writer for the name (same residual window the Cloudflare/RFC 2136 fixes accept). Fail-on-revert tests (backend_route53_test.go, rewritten onto a stateful `r53FakeAPI` that models GET-list + POST-change RRset semantics): `TestRoute53UpsertPreservesForeignRecord`, `TestRoute53RenumberPreservesForeign`, `TestRoute53DeletePreservesForeign` seed a co-resident foreign value and assert it SURVIVES publish/renumber/withdraw while xpf's value is set/renumbered/removed. Two-layer fix (the prior attempt #5388 did only layer 1 and REGRESSED the callers). LAYER 1 (backend, additive on #5387's StreamBGPRoutes which is untouched): `routeReader.GetRoutes`/`GetRoutesForTable`/`GetAllTableRoutes` (pkg/routing/routes.go) now `errors.Join` each per-family netlink failure into the returned error, tagged with the family (`inet`/`inet6` via new `familyName` helper) plus table id / routing-instance name, and STILL return the successful family's entries; `GetAllTableRoutes` joins the main-table + per-instance errors (previously `continue`d and dropped the whole instance table) while still appending every table it could read; `frr.GetRouteDetailJSON` (pkg/frr/status_parse.go) joins per-command vtysh + JSON-parse failures tagged with the failing `show ip/ipv6 route json` command.   **Action**: #5066 [BUG cli MEDIUM] `clear security flow session summary` (or `brief`, or `sort-by bytes`) parsed clean and cleared EVERY session on both HA nodes (fail-open destructive parse). The shared show/clear filter parser (`parseSessionFilter`, pkg/cli/session_filter.go) recognized the presentation tokens `summary`/`brief`/`sort-by` and set their display flags WITHOUT a parseErr, but `hasFilter()` deliberately excludes those three (they are display modifiers, not selectors), so on the clear path (`cli_clear.go` handleClearSecurity flow/session) `hasFilter()` returned false → `ClearAllSessions()` PLUS an unfiltered `clearPeerSessions(nil)` — the most destructive path — fired for a pasted show-syntax token. The remote `cli` clear parser (cmd/cli/clear.go) already rejected these via its `default` case; only the local interactive CLI was fail-open. Fix (selector-only clear parser, fail-closed): split `parseSessionFilter` into a shared `parseSessionFilterMode(args, clearMode bool)` with two entry points — `parseSessionFilter` (show, clearMode=false) and new `parseClearSessionFilter` (clear, clearMode=true). In clearMode the `summary`/`brief`/`sort-by` cases call `setParseErr(errDisplayModifierOnClear(tok))` instead of setting the display flag; `hasFilter()` already returns true when `parseErr != nil`, so a rejected token routes into `clearFilteredSessions` → `validate()` returns the error BEFORE any Iterate/Delete/ClearAll runs — neither clear method is invoked. `cli_clear.go` now calls `parseClearSessionFilter(args[2:])`. An EXACTLY-empty token list remains the only clear-all selector. Also hardened the SHOW path: `sort-by <value>` now validates the key is `bytes`|`packets` (an unknown value previously degraded silently to a plain per-session list instead of the requested top-talkers view) via a new parseErr surfaced through the existing showFlowSession `validate()`. Fail-on-revert tests (pkg/cli/cli_clear_flow_display_reject_test.go): a `clearCountDP` cliRuntime counts `ClearAllSessions`/`IterateSessions` calls; `TestClearFlowSessionRejectsDisplayModifiers` drives `clear security flow session {summary|brief|sort-by bytes|sort-by packets|protocol tcp summary}` and asserts each returns an error with BOTH counters at 0; `TestClearFlowSessionEmptyStillClearsAll` proves the no-arg path still calls ClearAllSessions exactly once; `TestParseClearSessionFilterRejectsDisplayTokens` asserts the clear parser sets parseErr/hasFilter/validate-error for the three tokens, the show parser still accepts them, and the show parser now rejects `sort-by garbage`. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: reverting the clear call site to `parseSessionFilter` made all five reject-subtests FAIL with output "0 IPv4 and 0 IPv6 session entries cleared" (and "matching sessions cleared" for the filter+summary case) — i.e. the destructive clear-all fired; restored → PASS. - - **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
  **Action**: #5121 [BUG lldp MEDIUM] The LLDP `Manager` lifecycle transitions `Apply` (config commit) and `Stop` (daemon shutdown) had NO lifecycle mutex. `Apply` wrote `m.cancel` and called `m.wg.Add(1)` per interface with no lifecycle lock; `Stop` read `m.cancel`, snapshotted `m.sessions`, and called `m.wg.Wait()`. Only `m.mu` guarded the neighbor table / sessions — nothing serialized `cancel`/`wg`/the session-publish-vs-snapshot across the two calls. The daemon shutdown path (`pkg/daemon/daemon_run.go` `runShutdownSequence`:904) calls `lldpMgr.Stop()` WITHOUT the `applySem` that `reconcileLLDP`->`Apply` (daemon_apply.go:2077) runs under, so a SIGTERM mid-commit races them: `wg.Add` vs `wg.Wait` (WaitGroup misuse — panic or dropped join), a data race on `m.cancel`, and a `Stop` that snapshots the session set before `Apply` publishes a later interface's session leaves that RX goroutine parked in `recv` forever (hangs shutdown / leaks the socket). Fix: a dedicated `lifecycleMu sync.Mutex` (distinct from `mu`) held by `Apply` across the whole teardown-then-rebuild and by `Stop` across teardown. Split the old `Stop` body into an internal `stopLocked()` (caller holds `lifecycleMu`); `Apply` calls `stopLocked()` (not `Stop`) to avoid re-acquiring the non-reentrant lock. `lifecycleMu` is never taken by the TX/RX/expiry goroutines (they take only `mu`), so holding it across `wg.Wait()` cannot deadlock. RED-on-revert VERIFIED under `-race`: reverting to the unguarded `Apply`(`m.Stop()`)/`Stop` made `TestApplyStopLifecycleRace` FAIL with WARNING: DATA RACE on `m.cancel` (Stop lldp.go:352) racing Apply's write + the WaitGroup/context internals, exit 1; restored -> `ok`. New test: pkg/lldp/lifecycle_mutex_5121_test.go (two goroutines hammer Apply/Stop 300x each, then assert coherent final teardown: not Running(), 0 sessions). Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; `go test -race ./pkg/lldp/...` ok; `go test -race -run LLDP ./pkg/daemon/` ok; gofmt clean. Docs: pkg/lldp/README.md gained an "Apply/Stop concurrency (#5121)" bullet + updated Apply/Stop entry-point lines. No cluster smoke (control-plane lifecycle race; no forwarding effect).
  **File(s)**: pkg/lldp/lldp.go, pkg/lldp/lifecycle_mutex_5121_test.go, pkg/lldp/README.md, _Log.md

Four swallow sites: `runtimeSourceNATPools` returned a bare `nil` on `provider.Status()` error (indistinguishable from provider-absent); the `natPoolStatsHandler` legacy `ReadNATPortCounter` fallback kept `used=0` on error (still HTTP 200); `natRuleStatsHandler` kept `hitPkts/hitBytes=0` on `ReadNATRuleCounter` error (still 200); gRPC `GetNATPoolStats` kept `used64=0` on `NATPortCounter` error and `GetNATRuleStats` returned `0,0` on `NATRuleCounter` error. A missing apply-id / absent runtime entry is a legitimate "no counter" and stays unflagged — the failure case is distinguishable (id resolves, telemetry call errors). Fix (fail closed as unavailable, per the #3345/#3408 counter-error contract already enforced on the zone/policy/filter surfaces): `runtimeSourceNATPools` now returns `(map, error)` and propagates a `Status()` read failure; `natPoolStatsHandler` returns HTTP 500 on that error AND on a fallback port-counter read failure; `natRuleStatsHandler` returns HTTP 500 on a rule-counter read failure. gRPC `GetNATPoolStats` returns `codes.Internal` on a `NATPortCounter` failure; `GetNATRuleStats`'s `readCounter` helper now returns an error that both source and destination call sites map to `codes.Internal`. Fail-on-revert tests: `pkg/api/nat_counter_error_test.go` (REST 500 on runtime-status/port-counter/rule-counter read failure + Prometheus omit-sample-and-bump) and `pkg/grpcapi/nat_counter_error_test.go` (gRPC codes.Internal on port/rule counter read failure). The gRPC mocks define their own `Telemetry()` routing through the mock (the embedded `*dataplane.Manager` has a promoted `Telemetry()` that would otherwise wrap the raw Manager and bypass the injected error). RED-on-revert VERIFIED: stashing the four source files made all 6 tests FAIL — REST handlers returned 200 with `used_ports:0`/`hit_packets:0`/`0.0%`, the collector left `counterReadErrors` at 0, and both RPCs returned nil error; restored → PASS.   **Action**: #5052 [BUG cli LOW] The read-only rollback DISPLAY selectors truncated an out-of-range index through int32 and silently rendered the WRONG rollback slot with a success exit. `show system rollback [compare] N` (cmd/cli/show_system.go) and `show | compare rollback N` (cmd/cli/show.go handleConfigShow) parsed the selector with `strconv.Atoi` then cast `int32(n)`. On this 64-bit target `strconv.Atoi("4294967297")` succeeds, passes the `n >= 1` check, then `int32(4294967297) == 1` — so the ShowRollback/ShowCompare RPC carried slot 1 while the operator asked for a different (invalid) selector; the server (ShowRollback/ShowCompare in pkg/grpcapi/server_config.go) only validates the already-truncated positive value and cannot reconstruct the pre-truncation int. The mutating `rollback N` path already had the `ParseInt(_,10,32)` guard (#4868/#3447 in shared.go); these three display paths were missed. Fix (per the issue's fix direction — one shared parser): added `parseRollbackSelector(token, usage, min) (int32, error)` in cmd/cli/shared.go — `strconv.ParseInt(token, 10, 32)` returns `strconv.ErrRange` for any value outside int32 range instead of wrapping; `min` is 0 for the mutating `rollback` (0 = revert to active) and 1 for the read-only display/compare selectors that need a positive slot. Refactored the mutating rollback case to call it (min=0) and wired all three display paths through it (min=1). The `int32(n)` casts on the RPC fields were dropped (the helper already returns int32). Fail-on-revert test (cmd/cli/show_rollback_int32_5052_test.go): a `showRollbackRecorderClient` records ShowRollback.N / ShowCompare.RollbackN; `TestShowRollbackDisplaySelectorOverflowNoRPC_5052` drives all three display paths with `4294967297`/`4294967296`/`2147483648`/`foo`/`0` and asserts each returns an error with the display RPC issued 0 times; `TestShowRollbackDisplaySelectorValidPassthrough_5052` proves valid slots (2, 3, and the MaxInt32 boundary 2147483647) pass through UNCHANGED. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: reverting show.go's compare-rollback site to `strconv.Atoi`+`int32()` made the three `show | compare rollback` overflow subtests FAIL — the truncated RollbackN=1 RPC was issued with a nil error (the other two paths, still fixed, kept passing, and the valid-passthrough tests kept passing) — restored → all PASS. Validation: `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0; `go test ./cmd/cli/... ./pkg/cli/...` all ok; gofmt clean. Docs: no doc change — valid selectors behave identically; the fix only converts a silent wrong-slot render into a clean rejection of an out-of-range/malformed selector, and the rollback CLI reference already documents `<N>` as a positive rollback index. No cluster smoke (control-plane CLI parse path; no forwarding change).

## 2026-07-10 — #5115 term-scoped next-hop-self

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: #5115 [BUG frr/bgp MEDIUM] `then next-hop self` widened into a
  neighbor-wide next-hop rewrite. `policy_render.go` scanned the effective
  export policy with `policyStatementHasNextHopSelf` and, if ANY term
  requested self, emitted `neighbor <peer> next-hop-self force` — an FRR knob
  that runs AFTER route selection and rewrites the next-hop of EVERY route
  advertised to the peer, including routes accepted by OTHER terms that never
  asked for self (semantic widening; can redirect traffic through the
  firewall or break third-party next-hop reachability). Fix: lower
  `then next-hop self` per-term INSIDE the export route-map as
  `set ip next-hop peer-address` + `set ipv6 next-hop peer-address`. In an
  OUTBOUND route-map `peer-address` resolves to the local session address
  (= self) and is evaluated per-route, so it rewrites ONLY the term's routes.
  Removed both neighbor-loop knob emissions (IPv4 + IPv6) and the now-unused
  `policyStatementHasNextHopSelf` helper. The outbound set-clause still
  overrides iBGP / route-reflector-reflected next-hops (keeps the #2977 fix),
  now correctly scoped; a bare `then next-hop self` term (no `from`) renders a
  match-all sequence and keeps neighbor-wide effect. Fail-on-revert tests
  (pkg/frr/frr_test.go): rewrote TestGenerateProtocols_BGPExportNextHopSelf
  and ...RRClient to assert the term-scoped set-clause + NO neighbor knob;
  added TestGenerateProtocols_BGPExportNextHopSelfTermScoped (the #5115
  two-accepted-term widening regression: prefix A accepted without self,
  prefix B accepted with self → exactly one set-clause, scoped to B's
  sequence, no knob); updated TestNextHopPeerAddress and
  ...BGPExportNoSpuriousNextHopSelf. RED-on-revert VERIFIED: restoring
  origin/master's policy_render.go (keeping the tests) made 4 tests FAIL
  (BGPExportNextHopSelf, ...RRClient, ...TermScoped, TestNextHopPeerAddress),
  no-spurious correctly stayed PASS; restored → all PASS. Validation:
  `GOCACHE=/dev/shm/cache GOTMPDIR=/dev/shm go build ./...` exit 0;
  `go test ./pkg/frr/... ./pkg/config/...` ok; gofmt clean. Docs:
  pkg/frr/README.md `next-hop self` section + docs/phases.md rewritten to the
  term-scoped route-map contract. No cluster smoke (control-plane FRR config
  generation; verified by RED-on-revert unit tests).

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix flowexport batch max-depth high-water update race (#5048).
  The `maxDepth` high-water update in `flowBatch.add()` ran OUTSIDE `b.mu`
  as a plain load-then-store (`if depth > maxDepth.Load() { Store(depth) }`),
  so two concurrent adders could interleave — B stores 2, A's later store
  of 1 clobbers it — regressing the published high-water mark. Replaced with
  a lock-free CAS-max loop (atomic `max(old, observed)`), consistent with the
  sibling `dropped`/`handoffDropped` atomics that also update outside mu.
  Added a test-only `maxDepthHook` seam and a deterministic barrier test that
  forces the reverse-order store (RED-on-revert: MaxDepth regresses 2->1) plus
  a 256-goroutine `-race` stress test. Docs: no contract change — maxDepth was
  already documented as a monotonic high-water mark; this only makes it correct
  under concurrency.
- **File(s)**: pkg/flowexport/transport.go,
  pkg/flowexport/maxdepth_race_5048_test.go

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: #5312 flowexport/ipfix — emit RECORD-granularity sampling IEs.
  ShouldExport does 1-in-N selection of whole SESSION records, but
  encodeIPFIXOptionsSamplerDataSet advertised PSAMP PACKET-selection IEs
  (selectorAlgorithm 304 / samplingPacketInterval 305 / samplingPacketSpace
  306, interval=1/space=N-1). A standards collector reads that as packet
  sampling and renormalizes each record's octet/packetDeltaCount by N —
  inflating the already-complete per-session volume. The only guard was a
  code comment ("must NOT multiply by N") that no wire field carried.
  Replaced with the RFC 7014 (Flow Selection Techniques) flow-selection IEs:
  flowSelectorAlgorithm (390, u16) = 1 (systematic count-based, IANA "Flow
  Selector Algorithm" registry), samplingFlowInterval (396, u64) = 1,
  samplingFlowSpacing (397, u64) = N-1. Record size 14 -> 22. A collector now
  scales the POPULATION (flow count/aggregate) by N and leaves per-record
  counters intact. Updated the sampler test to pin 390/396/397 + u64 widths +
  record size 22 AND assert 304/305/306 are ABSENT; proved RED-on-revert
  (reverting ipfix.go fails the template/data-set decode tests). Updated
  pkg/flowexport/README.md #3748/#5312 sampler section.

- **Action**: #5094 — ra join-timeout reclaimer no longer drops the owed
  replacement / terminal goodbye. Before the fix, when a draining sender's owner
  wedged past `claimWaitTimeout`, `releaseDrain` handed the tombstone to a
  detached reclaimer that merely `delete`d it once the wedged owner exited —
  losing the changed-config replacement (`onProvenClose`) and any owed
  standalone goodbye, so the interface could stay senderless (or lose its
  goodbye) until an unrelated later Apply re-drove it. Extracted the
  proven-close ordered decision (goodbye claim-once + replacement +
  supersession re-check) into `finishDrainDecision`; both `releaseDrain`'s
  `<-stopped` arm AND the reclaimer now run it — the reclaimer waits for
  `<-stopped` first (restoring the happens-before + old-conn-closed
  precondition) so all #2033 invariants hold (≤1 live conn, ordered emit,
  claim-once, epoch/ifaceEpoch supersession, entry-identity guard). Made
  `onProvenClose` a bare `startLocked` closure and moved the #2834
  make-before-break `waitConnReady` into `releaseDrain` to avoid a data race
  on Apply-local state now that the closure runs in the reclaimer goroutine.
  Added a `joinTimedOut` flag surfaced via `Manager.Status` / `show interfaces`
  ("draining (join timed out; reclaiming)"). RED-on-revert proven: reverting the

- **Action**: #5298 — install FRR reject/blackhole route for static-route
  reject/discard (fix the silently-erased `reject`). The schema
  (`schema_routing.go`) already accepted a `route <prefix> reject` leaf and
  `isRouteInlineKeyword` already treated `reject` as a clause boundary, but
  `StaticRoute` carried only `Discard` and neither the inline nor the
  hierarchical action switch in `compileStaticRoutes` handled `reject` — so a
  committed reject compiled to a no-next-hop, non-discard route, which the FRR
  renderer (post-#3872) deliberately renders as NOTHING, letting matching
  traffic fall through to a less-specific route (a security/vsrx-parity
  fail-wide). Added `StaticRoute.Reject`; handled `reject` in both action
  switches + the same-destination merge; taught `generateStaticRouteInTable`
  to emit `ip|ipv6 route <dst> reject [<pref>] [vrf/table]` (RTN_UNREACHABLE →
  ICMP unreachable) while `discard` keeps `Null0` (RTN_BLACKHOLE, silent).
  Folded `Reject` into the userspace AF_XDP FIB silent-drop snapshot
  (`buildRouteSnapshots`) so the fast path drops the prefix instead of
  LPM-matching a less-specific route; added `reject` display parity to CLI +
  gRPC `show route` and mirrored the `Discard` skip in daemon neighbor
  pre-resolution. Junos vs FRR semantics: Junos reject→FRR reject (ICMP),
  Junos discard→FRR Null0/blackhole (silent). Tests: end-to-end compile→FRR
  render (v4+v6, reject + discard) in pkg/frr, compiler-propagation (flat-set
  + hierarchical) in pkg/config; proved RED-on-revert (reverting the compiler
  reject cases and the render change fails the four reject tests while the
  discard guards stay green). Regenerated golden_4406 baseline (additive
  `Reject:false` field only, no behavior change). Build + touched-package
  tests green.

- **Action**: #5120 routing/wireguard — unbind the WG TUN from its VRF on
  teardown/rebind. `applyWireguardTunLocked` bound the persistent `wgN` TUN
  to a VRF only in the non-empty routing-instance case with no else/unbind
  branch, and the WG config-removal prune in `Apply` only reconciled
  addresses. So removing the `routing-instance` stanza from a still-
  configured tunnel — or removing the whole tunnel — left `wgN` mastered to
  the old `vrf-<name>` indefinitely (traffic isolated in / leaked through
  the wrong routing table). Routed WG through the SAME identity-gated claim
  machinery as GRE/IPIP: the apply path now calls `reconcileVRFClaimLocked`
  (records `appliedRI` on a successful bind, unbinds when the desired RI is
  empty), and the persistent-link removal prune calls the new extracted
  `unbindVRFClaimLocked` helper (identity-checks the current master vs the
  claimed `vrf-` device, LinkSetNoMaster only when it is ours, retains the
  claim + `wgConfigured` entry on transient failure for retry, clears on a
  not-found device). Preserved `appliedRI` across the non-WG→WG same-name
  handoff so a reused anchor TUN's prior VRF claim carries into the WG
  reconcile (else an anchor→WG-no-RI device would strand its old master).
  Added four fail-on-revert tests (bind+removal-unbind, RI-removal-unbind,
  foreign-master-veto, transient-unbind retry); proved RED-on-revert (3/4

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: #5123 pkg/lldp — withdraw a neighbor immediately on a TTL=0
  shutdown LLDPDU. The RX path stored a TTL=0 frame like any other neighbor
  (ExpiresAt==now), so a departed peer stayed visible in `Neighbors()` until
  the next ~10s `expiryLoop` tick, violating IEEE 802.1AB shutdown semantics
  (the receiver must delete the neighbor at once). `rxLoop` now computes the
  `ifname/chassis/port` key and, when the parsed TTL is 0, calls the new
  `withdrawNeighbor` helper — a locked delete under the same `mu` the learn
  and expiry paths use — and does NOT cache the frame. A TTL=0 frame for an
  unknown key is a no-op (no error, no spurious insert). The non-zero TTL
  learn/refresh path is unchanged and the 10s reap cadence is untouched.
  Added three fail-on-revert tests driving the real `rxLoop` through the
  `recvFn` seam with a deterministic synchronous handshake: immediate
  withdrawal after TTL=0, unknown-key no-insert, non-zero learn+refresh.
  Proved RED-on-revert (the two TTL=0 tests fail on reverted source; the
  refresh test passes both ways by design). `go test -race ./pkg/lldp/...`
  green. Updated pkg/lldp/README.md neighbor-lifecycle + ParseTLVs notes.

- **Action**: #5071 — preserve downstream giaddr + Option 82 on DHCP relay
  chaining (RFC 1542 §4.1.1 / RFC 3046). The forward loop stamped its own
  giaddr and Del/overwrote Option 82 unconditionally, even when the inbound
  BOOTREQUEST already carried a nonzero giaddr from a downstream relay —
  making the server pick the wrong pool, reply to the wrong relay, and
  destroying the original circuit-id. Added `giaddrIsSet()` and captured the
  chained condition BEFORE any mutation; on a chained request (giaddr!=0) the
  relay now preserves BOTH giaddr and the downstream relay-agent Option 82
  untouched and only increments the BOOTP hops field. First-hop path
  (giaddr==0) is unchanged: stamp giaddr + insert circuit-id Option 82. The
  RFC 1542 hop-limit check (#4309, default 16) runs for both paths. No new
  config knob (untrusted-client Option 82 trust policy noted out of scope).
  Three fail-on-revert tests (first-hop stamp preserved, chained
  giaddr+Option-82 preserved with exact-byte assertions, chained hop-limit
  drop); RED-on-revert proven (chained-preserve fails on reverted source,
  first-hop passes both ways). Updated pkg/dhcprelay/README.md with a "Relay
  chaining" section + first-hop-only Option 82 gotcha.

- **Action**: #5067 — bind `show firewall [filter <name>] effective` to the
  helper-acknowledged generation. The effective view compiled its snapshots
  from ActiveConfig() and labeled them as what "the dataplane actually
  receives" without ever consulting the apply/generation state. commitAndApply
  promotes the active config via store.Commit() BEFORE applyAndSyncCommitted
  runs; a required-protocol-gate apply error (applyErrSkipsPeerSync /
  compileErrorMustAbortApply) leaves the dataplane DISARMED while ActiveConfig
  is already the new generation, so the view falsely certified an unapplied
  config as live. Added firewallEffectiveLiveness (dataplane loaded + helper
  status → armed && acked-gen == last-applied-gen) and
  printFirewallEffectiveBanner: certifies "dataplane-acknowledged (generation
  N)" only when armed+coherent, else prints a prominent COMPILED-DESIRED /
  disarmed-or-drift banner surfacing acked vs desired generations; a soft note
  when no runtime is wired. Display-only — no change to apply/commit/sync.
  Applied to both the all-filters and single-filter forms. Four tests
  (armed-acked, disarmed-drift, generation-drift, no-runtime); RED-on-revert
  proven (the disarmed + drift tests fail on reverted source — the compiled
  snapshot is presented as effective with no banner). Updated

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10 (fix/5074-rollback-preflight-failclosed)
  - **Action**: #5074 fail the rollback preflight closed on non-ENOENT
    config-DB stat errors. `preflight` classified the DB dir with
    `os.Stat(...) == nil {snapshot} else {skip}`, so ANY non-ENOENT stat
    error (EACCES/EIO/stale mount) took the else branch, logged "no config
    DB", left `DBSnapshotPath` empty (`AdvancedStateFloor` false) and let
    the binary cut proceed with no restorable pre-upgrade DB. `dirSize`
    errors during space sizing were also silently ignored. Fix: branch the
    stat EXPLICITLY (nil -> present+snapshot; os.IsNotExist -> skip; ANY
    OTHER -> return error, abort the pure preflight before any live
    mutation) via an injectable `statConfigDBDir` seam; surface `dirSize`
    failures on a PRESENT DB. Clean abort (preflight is pure — no binary
    swap / marker / snapshot side-effect on the error path). New
    RED-on-revert tests (present/absent/EACCES/EIO/dirSize-error +
    Run-level no-mutation); RED proven (buggy code cuts to COMMITTED on
    EACCES). Updated docs/in-place-upgrade.md PREFLIGHT bullet.
  - **File(s)**: pkg/upgrade/cutover.go,
    pkg/upgrade/preflight_dbsnap_failclosed_5074_test.go,
    docs/in-place-upgrade.md, _Log.md

  - **Action**: #5428 fail safe on a dpkg-query error in the kernel

    a purge FAILURE / partial purge, but both the PRE-purge installed-set
    loop and the POST-purge confirmed-absent re-query used a helper that
    returned `false` on ANY dpkg-query error, so a dpkg-DB corruption/parse

## 2026-07-10 — #5455 tcp-flags operator-only fail-open fix
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5455 fail-open widening of a firewall filter. ParseTCPFlagsExpression now rejects a NON-EMPTY tcp-flags expression that sets no flag bits — operator-only ("&"), empty operand ("()"), and leading/trailing/duplicated "&" conjunctions ("& syn", "syn &", "syn && ack"). Added per-segment operand tracking (segHasFlag): a "&" with no flag operand on its left errors mid-loop; a final segment left empty errors after the loop; the historical `required==0 && forbidden==0 → (false,nil)` fall-through is now a fail-closed error. The legitimately-ABSENT case (expr=="" empty/whitespace) still returns (0,0,false,nil). Strict validator (validateFirewallTCPFlagsStrict) unchanged — it already rejects on err!=nil, so the new error makes "&"/"syn &" fail at commit instead of silently matching all TCP. Distinct from #4714 (dangling "!"). RED-on-revert proven: on origin/master "syn &" parses ok=true req=0x02 (drops trailing &); "&"/"()" return ok=false,nil (no constraint) and commit.
- **File(s)**: pkg/config/tcp_flags.go, pkg/config/tcp_flags_test.go, pkg/config/compiler_validate_strict_filter.go, pkg/config/README.md, _Log.md

- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5512 security fail-OPEN on the PRIMARY host-inbound path. The nft lo0 term lowering (nftRulesFromTerm, pkg/daemon/daemon_nft.go) handled an UNREPRESENTABLE tcp-flags expression by DROPPING the constraint with a slog.Warn and emitting the term's configured verdict — widening an accept-term to admit ALL TCP. Now fails the term CLOSED: on ParseTCPFlagsExpression err, set tcpFlagsFailClosed and emit a per-TERM terminating `<match> meta l4proto 6 drop` overriding the term action (accept→denied, discard/reject→still deny, fall-through/PBR→terminate-drop). Mirrors the userspace direction (filters.go TCPFlagsUnparseable → Rust SnapshotIntegrityError::UnrepresentableFilterTCPFlags) but per-TERM so it never rejects the whole atomically-loaded lo0 table (that would leave NO host filter = fail-open). `meta l4proto 6` scopes the drop to TCP (a tcp-flags constraint only ever matches TCP in per_packet_l4_matches), so a tcp-flags-only term does not lower to a bare drop that denies ALL host-inbound traffic. Added tests: TestNftRuleFromTermTCPFlagsUnrepresentableFailsClosed (RED-on-revert proven: reverted arm emits `meta l4proto 6 accept`, the widen), TestLo0FilterPayloadUnrepresentableTCPFlagsParses (nft -c -f - parses the emission cleanly — no syntax error, no whole-ruleset failure). Full pkg/daemon suite green.

## 2026-07-10 — #5062 eventengine supersede producer-race fix
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5062 concurrency data-race / data-structure-integrity bug in the event-options action queue. HandleEvent evaluates under e.mu but RELEASES it before enqueue, so many RPM-probe goroutines run enqueue concurrently. On a full 64-slot queue enqueue falls into supersede(), which DRAINS accepted actions into a private slice (opening slots) then re-enqueues survivors; with no producer lock a second producer (enqueue fast-path send OR its own supersede) took a drain-freed slot between the drain and the re-enqueue, forcing supersede's refill `default` branch to DROP a survivor — an already-accepted action for a DIFFERENT policy — losing it + its FIFO position (miscounted queue_full). Fix: new e.enqueueMu serializes ALL producer-side queue mutation, held across the WHOLE enqueue (fast-path send AND supersede drain+refill), so the drain→re-enqueue is atomic w.r.t. other producers; the only concurrent actor left is the consumer (actionWorker, removes only), so a drain-freed slot is re-filled only by supersede itself → every survivor preserved exactly once in FIFO order. Lock ordering: enqueueMu is a producer-only leaf lock, NEVER held while e.mu is held (enqueue runs after evaluateEvent released e.mu) and the worker path (staleReason/armCooldown take e.mu) never takes enqueueMu → no cycle, no deadlock (channel ops under enqueueMu are non-blocking select+default). Added test-only afterDrainFn seam (nil in prod). Tests: TestSupersede_ConcurrentProducersConserveSurvivors (concurrent barrier: 64 producers × 40 rounds, conservation+FIFO) and TestSupersede_DrainStealWindowIsClosed (deterministic drain→steal→drop reproduction). RED-on-revert proven: removing enqueueMu drops a survivor (steal displaces seed63 deterministically; concurrent test loses+reorders seeds). Full pkg/eventengine -race suite green, new tests 10× flake-clean. Distinct from #2869 (same-policy ordering, not concurrent capacity theft).
- **File(s)**: pkg/eventengine/engine.go, pkg/eventengine/engine_supersede_race_5062_test.go, pkg/eventengine/README.md, _Log.md

## 2026-07-10 — #5047 fabric-listener supervision (retry + health)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5047 control-plane liveness gap: RunFabricListener (pkg/grpcapi/server.go) treated an lc.Listen failure as TERMINAL (return) and its Serve goroutine only slog.Warn'd while the owner blocked on ctx.Done — so a transient bind/device error OR a later Serve fault PERMANENTLY removed the network-exposed peer-proxy gRPC surface (monitor / peer-show / proxied-failover) until the whole cluster-comms lifecycle restarted; single-fabric deployments had no fallback. Rewrote it as a supervisor loop (superviseFabricListener) mirroring the project's monitorFabricState/runFabricStateSubscription pattern: bind → serve → on a fault (bind failure OR a Serve error that is NOT ctx-cancel/grpc.ErrServerStopped) retry after a BOUNDED exponential backoff (100ms base, 5s cap, reset to base after a Serve that stayed up >=30s) while ctx is live — keeps retrying a persistent bind failure at the cap without spinning, never gives up permanently. Expected graceful shutdown (ctx cancel → serveUntilDone returns nil; grpc.ErrServerStopped via errors.Is) exits cleanly, no retry. No goroutine outlives ctx (reuses serveUntilDone's buffered-errCh worker + bounded stopGRPCServer). Extracted buildFabricServer() (the #4107 auth + #4122 allowlist interceptor chains) and the fabricSupervisorConfig listen/serve seams for injection. Published per-bind up/down health via setFabricListenerUp / FabricListenerUp(addr) / FabricListenerHealth() for a status surface; transitions log at Info(up/stopped)/Warn(bind-fail/serve-fault), retry ticks at Debug (logging rules). Caller (daemon_ha_sync.go:582,585) unchanged — signature identical, supervision is internal. Tests (server_fabric_listener_5047_test.go, -race): (a) transient bind failures → REAL serve path (buildFabricServer+serveUntilDone over bufconn) recovers, health down→up; (b) ctx-cancel → supervisor + serve worker exit promptly, no leak, listen called once; (c) grpc.ErrServerStopped (wrapped) → clean exit, NOT retried; (d) persistent bind failure → bounded backoff, retry count under window/cap bound (no spin). RED-on-revert proven: patching the loop back to the pre-#5047 terminal return makes (a) [never comes up] and (d) [only 1 attempt] FAIL. Full pkg/grpcapi + pkg/daemon -race suites green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/grpcapi/server.go, pkg/grpcapi/server_fabric_listener_5047_test.go, pkg/grpcapi/README.md, _Log.md

## 2026-07-10 — #5032 SNMPv3 privacy salt uniqueness (monotonic counter)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5032 (codex-review-177 [A9-b1-F10], Low): SNMPv3 privacy
  parameters were INDEPENDENT random draws (`rand.Read(privParams)` per call in
  `encryptDES`/`encryptAES128`) with no per-key uniqueness state, so IV
  uniqueness was only birthday-bound — RFC 3826 §3.1.2.1/§3.3 (AES) and
  RFC 3414 §8.1.1.1 (DES) require the salt to be UNIQUE per (engineBoots,key).
  A DES-CBC IV = pre-IV XOR salt repeat leaks first-block structure; an
  AES-128-CFB IV = boots||time||salt repeat leaks plaintext XORs. Replaced the
  per-message random draw with a MONOTONIC 64-bit salt counter
  (`Agent.nextPrivSalt`, v3.go): seeded ONCE from crypto/rand (via the `randRead`
  seam) at first use — arbitrary boot-time start per RFC 3826 §3.3 — then
  incremented atomically (`privSalt atomic.Uint64`) for each encryption, so
  successive salts within an engine boot are guaranteed distinct, not merely
  probably distinct. `encryptPDU` allocates the salt and threads it into
  `encryptDES(privKey,data,salt)` / `encryptAES128(privKey,data,salt,boots,time)`
  (signatures changed to take the salt explicitly, return just ciphertext+err;
  caller echoes the salt as wire privParams). Preserved the RFC IV construction
  (preIV^salt for DES, boots||time||salt for AES) and the #5453 fail-closed
  guarantee — relocated to the seed: if the one-time seed draw fails,
  nextPrivSalt errors, encryptPDU propagates, buildV3Response drops the datagram
  (never a zero/predictable-salt PDU). Thread-safe: one-time seed under
  `privSaltMu`, each allocation a single atomic increment (concurrent response +
  trap encryption never collide). engineBoots (immutable per boot, monotonic
  across restarts) scopes the counter so a reboot re-randomizes the start.
  Tests: new v3_priv_salt_5032_test.go — TestPrivSaltMonotonicUnique (strict +1
  monotonic + uniqueness over 100k), TestEncryptPDUDistinctSaltsPerMessage
  (end-to-end via encryptPDU, +1 monotonic privParams over 2k),
  TestPrivSaltConcurrentUnique (16×5000 goroutines, all distinct, -race clean).
  Rewrote v3_rand_failclosed_test.go to assert fail-closed at the new seed layer
  (TestPrivSalt_RNGFailClosed, TestBuildV3Response_RNGFailClosed with a fresh
  never-seeded agent) + supplied-salt roundtrip/length-validation. Updated
  callers in agent_test.go, v3_seclevel_test.go, v3_priv_iv_test.go to the new
  signature (shared testPrivSalt helper). RED-on-revert PROVEN: patching
  nextPrivSalt back to an independent random draw makes both monotonic tests FAIL
  at i=1. `go build ./...` + `go test ./pkg/snmp/...` (and -race subset) green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/snmp/v3.go, pkg/snmp/agent.go, pkg/snmp/v3_priv_salt_5032_test.go,
  pkg/snmp/v3_rand_failclosed_test.go, pkg/snmp/agent_test.go,
  pkg/snmp/v3_seclevel_test.go, pkg/snmp/v3_priv_iv_test.go, pkg/snmp/README.md, _Log.md
## 2026-07-10 — #5064 EventBuffer drop-visibility (seq + overrun + metric)
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5064 forensic-observability gap in the EventBuffer fan-out. `Add` fanned out non-blocking and took `default: // drop if subscriber is slow` on a full subscriber channel with NO counter, NO status, and NO sequence on the delivered record — a slow REST-SSE / gRPC event-stream / CLI-monitor consumer silently lost security/audit records and a forensic reader could not tell a gapped stream from a complete one. Fix adds three independent, in-band loss signals. (1) BufSeq: `Add` now stamps the buffer's monotonic publish sequence (`eb.seq`, from 1) onto every record BEFORE storing/fanning out — the SAME value stored in the ring, so a live subscriber and a `Latest()` snapshot agree; a BufSeq discontinuity between two delivered records pinpoints exactly which records were shed. Distinct from the reader-scoped `EventSeq` (#4915), which is 0 for the direct `Add` callers (health probes, HA replay). (2) Drop counters: per-subscriber `Subscription.dropped` (`atomic.Uint64`, accessor `Dropped()`) and aggregate `EventBuffer.droppedTotal` (accessor `DroppedTotal()`) increment on the drop path — no slog in the per-record path (CLAUDE.md logging rule). (3) Overrun flag: the fan-out arms a per-subscriber `overrun atomic.Bool` on a drop and stamps `EventRecord.Overrun=true` on the next successfully delivered record (per-subscriber copy so it is subscriber-scoped), giving a consumer that is not tracking BufSeq an explicit in-band "you lost records" signal; cleared once delivered. Exported the aggregate as Prometheus `xpf_event_stream_subscriber_dropped_total` (new `xpfCollector.eventStreamSubscriberDropped` desc, Describe+Collect emit guarded by `srv.eventBuf != nil`; declared-but-conditional emit is safe under the pedantic descriptor-coverage canary). Fan-out mutation is race-free (atomics; RLock unchanged). RED-on-revert PROVEN: restoring the old no-op `default` branch + dropping the BufSeq stamp fails `TestEventBufferDropVisibility` (sub.Dropped()=0, want 3). Gates: `go build ./...` green, `go test ./pkg/logging/... ./pkg/api/...` green, `-race` on the new tests green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/logging/eventbuf.go, pkg/logging/eventbuf_drop_visibility_5064_test.go, pkg/logging/README.md, pkg/api/metrics.go, pkg/api/metrics_descriptors.go, pkg/api/metrics_system.go, _Log.md
## 2026-07-10 — #5414 dhcp-relay untrusted client-forged giaddr / Option 82 anti-spoofing
- **Timestamp**: 2026-07-10
- **Action**: Fix #5414 (RFC 3046 §2.1). The #5071 chained-relay path trusted ANY nonzero inbound giaddr as a downstream-relay stamp and preserved it + its Option 82. Because the relay listens on a CLIENT-facing interface, a host on the client segment could forge a nonzero giaddr + crafted Option 82 to impersonate a downstream relay and steer the server's pool/policy selection (circuit-id/remote-id) or its reply. Fixed the trust point at pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go: gated the `chained` (preserve) decision on a new per-group trust flag — `chained := ir.trustOption82 && giaddrIsSet(...)`; `forgedGiaddr := !ir.trustOption82 && giaddrIsSet(...)`. On the DEFAULT untrusted interface a forged giaddr now falls through to the first-hop branch, which overwrites giaddr with the relay's own address (RFC 951/1542) and re-stamps Option 82 (addOption82 Dels the forged option first). The reset is counted in the new RelayStats.RequestsUntrustedGiaddrReset, incremented in the reset branch AFTER the hop-limit drop so a looping request is not miscounted. Added the Junos-parity config knob `overrides trust-option-82` (DHCPRelayGroup.TrustOption82) — compiled from all three parse shapes (flat-set/merged-Keys/block form), threaded through relaySpec.trustOption82 (participates in equal(), so a change restarts the relay) and interfaceRelay.trustOption82, and registered in setSchema for completion. ENFORCED, so no accepted-only advisory. Multi-hop relay preserved: on a trusted uplink (trust-option-82) the #5071 preserve behavior is intact. Tests: TestRunRelay_UntrustedForgedGiaddrOverwritten + _ResetCounted (pkg/dhcprelay) + TrustOption82 flat-set/default/merged+block/completion (pkg/config). RED-on-revert proven: reverting the trust-point to `chained := giaddrIsSet(...)` makes both new dhcprelay tests FAIL (giaddr + forged Option 82 preserved; counter 0) while the trusted #5071 preserve test still PASSES. Updated the #5071 chained test to drive the preserve path with a trusted config. `go build ./...` + `go test ./pkg/dhcprelay/... ./pkg/config/...` green.
- **File(s)**: pkg/dhcprelay/relay.go, pkg/dhcprelay/relay_chain_5071_test.go, pkg/config/types_system.go, pkg/config/compiler_services.go, pkg/config/schema_routing.go, pkg/config/compiler_dhcp_relay_overrides_test.go, pkg/dhcprelay/README.md, _Log.md
